title: The Healthy Eating Pyramid and Health Star Rating
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches the general concept of health promotion through education, environments and policy, not the Healthy Eating Pyramid or the Health Star Rating, so it is a different idea and the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Healthy Eating Pyramid and Health Star Rating
card: The Healthy Eating Pyramid shows how much of each food group to eat. Foods in the bigger, lower sections should be eaten most, and foods at the top the least.
Plant foods such as vegetables, fruit, legumes and wholegrain breads and cereals make up the wide base. Healthy fats and oils, lean meat, fish, eggs and dairy sit in the middle and upper sections.
The Health Star Rating is a label on the front of packaged food. It gives a rating from half a star to five stars.
More stars mean a healthier choice when comparing similar packaged foods, such as two breakfast cereals. It does not compare very different foods, such as a cereal and a yoghurt.
draft.remember: The Pyramid shows how much of each food group to eat. Stars compare similar packaged foods.

a.q: Where would the Healthy Eating Pyramid place vegetables, fruit and wholegrains?
opts: In the wide base, to be eaten the most
In the middle, to be eaten in small amounts
At the top, to be eaten the least
Outside the Pyramid, as they are not needed
a.why: The Pyramid puts plant foods in the wide base, because the bigger sections show the foods to eat most. The top is for foods to eat least, so plant foods do not belong there.
a.clue: A bigger section means more of that food.

b.q: Leila is choosing between two brands of muesli bars at a shop in Bendigo. One has 4 stars and the other has 2 stars. How should she use the Health Star Rating?
opts: Choose the 4 star bar as the healthier of the two bars
Choose the 2 star bar as it must have fewer kilojoules
Treat both bars as equal, as the stars only show size
Choose the 4 star bar as it is healthier than an apple
b.why: The Health Star Rating compares similar packaged foods, and more stars mean a healthier choice. It does not compare different foods, so a 4 star bar cannot be said to beat fresh fruit.
b.clue: Stars work best when the foods are of the same type.

a.best: In the wide base, to be eaten the most

b.best: Choose the 4 star bar as the healthier of the two bars

check.summary: No problems found. The Pyramid layers and the Health Star Rating range (half a star to five, comparing similar packaged foods) are accurate, and both questions have a single clear answer.
